newsitem.title: UK: British media highlights political leaders' wives.
newsitem.headline: British media highlights political leaders' wives.

text.p: LONDON, March 20 - With Britain's general election campaign barely under way, the nation's press and television have already highlighted the contrasting styles of the wives of Prime Minister John Major and Labour leader Tony Blair.
Most newspapers and TV channels focused on Thursday on the first public appearance together of the leading ladies, Norma Major and Cherie Blair.

While their husbands battled in parliament over a committee report on political sleaze, photographs of the two women sharing a laugh together at a bravery awards luncheon were splashed across the front pages of the nation's press.
"Ladies who laugh take their minds off May Day," said the tabloid Daily Mail headline of Wednesday's lunch.
"Their husbands may be engaged in a bitter political struggle, but Cherie Blair and Norma Major saw the funny side yesterday," another tabloid, the Express, commented.

British political wives were previously relegated to the sidelines but in 1997 no detail in the life of a present or future leader is too inconsequential to be reported in the run-up to the May 1 election.

Veteran political wife and country housewife Norma Major was deemed to have won the style war in her smart fuschia suit, while working mother and top lawyer Cherie Blair, 10 years her junior, was criticised for her more casual black trouser suit. Diana, Princess of Wales, Britain's most famous clothes horse, was also at the lunch.

"The consensus in the lunch-hour crowd outside the hotel was that Mrs Blair still had much to learn from the princess and Mrs Major about how to dress like a first lady," said the broadsheet Daily Telegraph, which featured photographs of all three women as their arrived for the ceremony at a London hotel.
Although it was only their third meeting, the two women -- who are poles apart politically -- shared a joke and an animated conversation.
The ruling Conservatives, who are trailing Labour by up to 25 percentage points in opinon polls, have called mother-of-two Norma their secret weapon and a sure vote-winner among the middle class.

Cherie Blair, an ambitious barrister and mother of three who has combined a busy family life and successful career, is likely to attract the younger voters in tune with her modern lifestyle and views.
"Mrs Blair is beautiful...but she looks like she's trying too hard," said an onlooker as the wives arrived. "Mrs Major looks more like a prime minister's wife."
